title: Packers suspect Edgerrin Cooper's Achilles injury will end his season
dek: Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered a non-contact Achilles injury during Sunday's game against Tampa Bay and was immediately ruled out. Head Coach Matt LaFleur said the injury appears season-ending, though final evaluation is ongoing.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Edgerrin Cooper suffered a non-contact Achilles injury in the third quarter of Sunday's game and LaFleur suspects it will end his season, pending full evaluation.
bottom_line: The final extent of Cooper's Achilles injury will be determined by the Packers' ongoing medical evaluation, which the team has not yet publicly concluded. How McDuffie and the linebacker rotation perform against Chicago this week will indicate whether Green Bay can absorb the loss without significant defensive regression.
body:
Through the first 2.5 quarters, he had compiled a team-high nine tackles, a sack, and an interception, per Packers.com. His loss removes a productive and established defensive presence from the Packers' linebacker group.
Isaiah McDuffie replaced Cooper at linebacker following the injury. McDuffie is a six-year pro with 40 NFL starts under his belt, according to Packers.com. LaFleur expressed confidence in the depth options available: Ty'Ron Hopper is viewed as a young, improving talent, and Zaire Franklin, a veteran newcomer to the linebacker corps, brings leadership and communication skills that will help the defense adjust, per Packers.com.
The Packers enter their next contest at 2-2 and will face the defending NFC North champion Chicago Bears, who are 3-1. The Bears will start backup quarterback Tyson Bagent in place of the injured Caleb Williams. Green Bay lost to the Bears twice in their final two regular-season games last year, with the second loss eliminating them in the playoffs.
